Subject: Production: sudden p99 latency spike and 502s on Redwood streams

Hi Neha / Sean,

We started seeing a large regression this morning around 09:05 PDT — sustained p99 latency for model streaming jumped from ~350ms to >2.1s and our checkout throughput collapsed. Around the same time we observed 502s from Redwood client calls in our logs. This is affecting all users in our US region and causing checkout failures.

Attached: edgeworks_syslog_tail.txt (tail with request ids) and p99-traces.zip (linked stack traces & tracer sampling).

What we observed:
- Spike in client-side errors (502) coincident with high token-latency in server traces.
- Error pattern suggests streaming response parsing failures on our side (client SDK), but traces show mixed framing where metadata headers appear inside the first data frame.

Can you confirm whether there were any runtime changes deployed on Redwood today? We need an urgent triage — timeline, recommended mitigation, and ETA for a fix.

Priyanka

Subject: RE: Production: sudden p99 latency spike and 502s on Redwood streams

Quick triage notes (runtime + SDK leads):

- Reproduced symptom locally with customers approximate workload (large prefix + streaming response). We saw metadata frames (the per-response metadata header blob) arriving partially inside the first data chunk when the client-side TCP frames coalesce above ~16KB.
- Our SDKs streaming parser expects a clear metadata boundary preceding payload frames. When boundary bytes are split across packetization, the parser can mis-interpret the metadata as body data, which then causes the client to attempt to parse body bytes and drop the proper KV cache updates. The server sees a repeated replay and the router applies backpressure — net result: token latency and elevated error rates.

Root cause hypothesis: a change in the chunk coalescing heuristics in the runtime + a previously latent SDK parser edgecase (boundary-scan across aggregated frames) surfaced under heavier payload sizes. Not a model regression.

Immediate mitigation (recommended):
1) EdgeWorks: toggle the client SDK to disable continuous batching / set max-chunk-size=8192 as a temporary workaround (we will provide a config snippet).
2) Redwood: push a short-lived router tweak to avoid coalescing metadata and data frames for responses that include a metadata blob >512 bytes.

Planned fix: SDK patch to make the boundary scanner resilient to cross-chunk splits + runtime tweak to preserve strong metadata delimiters. Ill open a PR with a test harness that reproduces the failure. ETA for SDK patch: ~6-8 hours to get a canary build; runtime-safe rollout within 24h if canary passes.

Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/EW-1245 (Jira), PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/578

Subject: Escalation: EdgeWorks production outage — exec sync request (14:30 PDT)

Vivek / Sean — were seeing an active customer outage impacting EdgeWorks checkouts (multiple merchants). Karthik's triage points to a client SDK boundary parsing issue interacting with our recent router chunk coalescing change.

Actions taken so far:
- Karthik has validated reproducer and provided temporary mitigation guidance (client config + runtime guard).
- We prepared a canary PR for the SDK and a runtime guard tweak that avoids metadata coalescing (links above).
- Customer applied temporary client config and saw immediate reduction in 502s — request latency is improving but not fully recovered.

Required from leadership:
- Exec sync with customer at 14:30 PDT (please confirm availability).
- Authorization to grant EdgeWorks a goodwill credit for the incident (suggest 50% credit for the affected day's usage) and a committed follow-up (postmortem + remediation plan).

I will run the call with the customer and Karthik will present technical details. Priyanka: letting you know were lining up the execs and will provide an interim communiqué for your merchants if approved.
